name: SND@LHC
full_name: Scattering and Neutrino Detector at the Large Hadron Collider
summary: SND@LHC is a compact collider-neutrino experiment in the TI18 tunnel, probing a very forward angular region complementary to FASER and especially sensitive to neutrinos from charm decays.
physics_targets: High-energy neutrino interactions of all three flavours
Forward charm production and very small momentum fractions
detection_principle: Tungsten-emulsion targets resolve neutrino vertices and charged-lepton signatures, while scintillating-fibre tracking and an iron-scintillator hadron calorimeter provide electronic measurements and muon identification. Upstream vetoes reject the intense muon flux.

sites.name: Switzerland; TI18 tunnel at the CERN LHC
sites.location: Switzerland; TI18 tunnel at the CERN LHC

status.label: Run 3 exposure complete / LS3 and upgrade preparations
status.evidence: CERN confirms Run 3 collision physics ended in June 2026 and LS3 began on 29 June. The collaboration programme and analyses continue, with an approved Run 4 upgrade described in the 2026 primary paper.

timeline.event: Installed and commissioned for LHC Run 3
LHC Run 3 exposure ended before Long Shutdown 3.

key_parameters.name: Location
key_parameters.value: TI18 tunnel, approximately 480 m from ATLAS

key_parameters.name: Hybrid detector
key_parameters.value: Tungsten-emulsion target, scintillating fibres and muon/hadron detector

phases.name: SND@LHC Run 3
phases.description: Tungsten-emulsion target, scintillating-fibre tracker and downstream electronic detector operated during the 2022-2026 LHC Run 3 exposure.

phases.name: SND@HL-LHC / approved Run 4 upgrade
phases.description: Upgrade approved in June 2025. A fully electronic detector replaces emulsion and adds magnetic analysis; the collaboration name remains SND@LHC. The 2026 paper studies installation scenarios rather than reporting Run 4 data.

results.summary: Observed neutrino interactions without a final-state muon with 6.4-sigma significance, using 2022-2023 collision data.
Published muon-background measurements covering proton and heavy-ion operation through 2025.

science_scope: The record describes the named experiment as one programme; detector subsystems and repeated analyses are not counted as independent experiments.
